title: Read-only Claude refusal for a denied for-loop names the loop rule, not the rule its body command broke
outcome:
When the read-only Claude gate denies a `for NAME in …; do …; done` line, the refusal names only the loop shape: "the only loop allowed is …, and every command in its body must pass on its own; run a body command alone to see the rule it breaks". It does not name the rule the body broke, for example `git -C` in `for d in a b; do git -C $d status; done`.

Fix direction: when the header and clauses parse (claude_bash_top_level_semicolon_clauses, the literal checks), expand the body the way claude_bash_literal_for_loop_is_read_only does, and return claude_bash_refusal_rule for the first failing expansion. Fall back to the shape rule otherwise.
acceptance: A denied well-formed literal for-loop whose body breaks a rule is refused with that body rule named; a malformed loop keeps the shape rule; tests cover both.
The full five-stage gate passes on the reviewed tree, and the review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher.
